source_text:
1 Kor 16,2 Μίαν σαββάτων, ἡ ἀναστάσιμος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμέρα, θησαυρίζετε
οὖν παρ' ἑαυτοῖς ὃ ἐὰν ἡ δύναμις ὑμῶν ἀποθέσθαι δύναται, ἀλύπως καὶ ἄνευ ἀνάγκης, ἵνα ἑτοίμους ὑμᾶς πρὸς τὴν δόσιν ἐπιδημήσας εὕρω, ἵνα μὴ ἐληλυθότος μου ἀρχὴ τοῦ εὐτρεπίζειν τὰ πρὸς τὴν κοινωνίαν γένηται. 1 Kor 16,8-9 Ἐν Ἐφέσῳ οὖν ταύτην ἔγραψε Κορινθίοις τὴν ἐπιστολήν. λέγει δὲ ἐκεῖ περιμένειν διὰ εὔλογον αἰτίαν· θύρα γὰρ ὑπερέχουσα καὶ πάνυ ἐνεργοῦσα εἰς τοὺς ἀκροατὰς ἀνέῳκται αὐτῷ· ὅθεν πολλοὺς εἶχε τοὺς ἀντικειμένους δαίμονας ἀλητηρίους καὶ ἀνθρώπους γόητας καὶ ἀπαταιῶνας· τότε γὰρ οἱ πονηροὶ πολλοὶ γίνονται ἐν τῷ ἀντικεῖσθαι, ὅταν ὁρῶσιν ἰσχύοντα τὸν λόγον τῆς πίστεως ἐν τοῖς παραδεχομένοις· ἔθος δὲ αὐτῷ τὴν παρρησίαν τοῦ τῆς εὐσεβείας λόγου θύραν καλεῖν. 1 Kor 16,10-11 Ὅταν βέβαιοι καὶ ἀμετακίνητοι ὦσι περὶ τὴν εὐσέβειαν οἱ παιδευόμενοι, ἀφόβως ἐπιδημοῦσιν αὐτοῖς οἱ διδάσκαλοι, οὐ δεδεκότες μή τις ῥᾳθυμία περὶ τοὺς ἀκροατὰς ὑπάρχῃ. διό φησι· προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς, ἵνα θαρρήσῃ Τιμόθεος ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, οὐ φοβηθείς, μὴ μετατραπῆτε. τούτῳ τῷ σημαινομένῳ ἐκ τοῦ φοβεῖσθαι συνεχρήσατο, καὶ ἐν τῇ ἑξῆς ἐπιστολῇ εἶπεν· φοβοῦμαι μή πως, ὡς ὁ ὄφις ἐξηπάτησε τὴν Εὔαν ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτοῦ, οὕτως φθαρῇ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν. Ἔστι γὰρ ὁ Τιμόθεος οὗτος περὶ οὗ γράφω τὰ προκείμενα, τῶν γνησίων τοῦ θεοῦ δοῦλος, τὸ ἔργον τοῦ δεσπότου παραπλησίως ἐμοὶ ἐργαζόμενος. διὸ μὴ εὐτελιζέσθω παρ' ὑμῶν, ἀλλὰ γνησίως μετ' ἀγάπης ὑποδεχθήτω, ἀλλὰ καὶ προπεμφθήτω· περιμένω γὰρ ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ ἕως ἐπανέλθῃ πρός με μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν. 1 Kor 16,12 Ἐπειδὴ ὁ Ἀπολλῶς ἐπίσκοπος ἦν Κορίνθου, ἀπέστη ἐξ αὐτῶν διὰ τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς σχίσματα καὶ ἦν σὺν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ νῦν παρακληθεὶς οὐ συνεξεδήμησε τῇ ἐπιστολῇ· καὶ λέγει τὴν αἰτίαν δι' ἣν οὐκ ἀπῆλθεν· 13 ὅτι οὐκ ἦν θέλημα. εἶτα εὐθυμοποιῶν αὐτοὺς γράφει· ἐλεύσεται δὲ ὅταν εὐκαιρήσῃ, τὴν εὐκαιρίαν τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιδημίας αὐτοῦ ὑμῶν παρεχόντων, ὅταν μηκέτι ᾖ ἐν ὑμῖν σχίσματα. 1 κορ 16,13 Ἕπεται τῷ δεόντως ἐγρηγορότι ἐν τῷ μὴ διδόναι ὕπνον τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς μηδὲ ἐπινυσταγμὸν τοῖς βλεφάροις τὸ ἑστάναι βεβαίως ἐν τῇ πίστει, μεθ' ὃ ἕπεται τὸ ἀνδρίζεσθε καὶ κραταιοῦσθε ὡς ἀθλητῇ καὶ στρατιώτῃ Χριστοῦ, τῷ πάντα ποιοῦντι σὺν ἀγάπῃ τῇ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ τὸν πλησίον. 1 Kor 16,14-16 Ἀπαρχὴ λέγονται ἢ διὰ τὸ πρὸ τῶν ἄλλων πεπιστευκέναι ἢ διὰ τὸ ὑπερέχειν ἐν εὐσεβείᾳ ἢ διὰ τὸ προύχειν ἐν γένει, οἵτινες διὰ τὴν ἐνυπάρχουσαν αὐτοῖς ταπεινοφροσύνην οὐ χειροτονηθέντες, ἀλλὰ προθέσει ἰδίᾳ ὑφ' ἑαυτῶν εἰς τοῦτο ἠγμένοι, ἔταξαν ἑαυτοὺς εἰς διακονίαν. διὸ ὑποτάσσεσθε τοῖς τοιούτοις, εἰκόνα καὶ ὑπογραμμὸν αὐτοὺς ἔχοντες, ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἑαυτοὺς τάξητε εἰς τὴν τῶν ἁγίων ὑπηρεσίαν. 1 Kor 16,17-18 Σὺν τῷ Στεφανᾷ τὸ παραλειφθὲν ὑμῖν ἀνεπλήρωσαν Φουρτουνᾶτος καὶ Ἀχαϊκὸς τῆς αὐτῆς ἐκείνῳ προαιρέσεως ὄντες, καὶ ἀνέπαυσαν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ὑμῶν καὶ τὸ ἐμόν. ἀναπαύει δὲ πνεῦμα ἁγίου ὁ φρονῶν καὶ πράττων τὰ τῆς εὐσεβείας· τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα τὰ ἀγαθὰ ζητεῖ ὡς εἶναι· ἐπὶ μὲν φαύλων ψυχήν, ἐπὶ δὲ ἁγίων πνεῦμα λέγεσθαι τὸ ὑπερπηδοῦν ἐν τῷ τὰ καλὰ θέλειν. τοὺς οὖν εὐβιοῦντας καὶ φρονοῦντας ἐπιγινώσκειν δεῖ τῷ τὰ αὐτὰ φρονεῖν καὶ πράττειν. οὕτω καὶ ὁ Ὠριγένης δοξάζει τὸ πνεῦμα πλείω τι ἔχειν τῆς ψυχῆς ἐν ἀρετῇ, εἰ καὶ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ ψυχή. 1 Kor 16,19- Ἱκανῶς αὐτοὺς εἰς ἀγάπην διεγείρων γράφει τὸ ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῆς Ἀσίας καὶ πάντες οἱ ἐν αὐτῇ διατρίβοντες ἅγιοι καὶ εὐλαβεῖς ἄνδρες. 1 Kor 16,21 Ἵνα μὴ ἀπατῶνται γραφόντων τινῶν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ 4 ἀποστόλου προσηγορίας, σημεῖον τοῦτο τῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπιστολῶν ποιεῖται τὸ 14 χειρὶ τῇ ἑαυτοῦ κεχαρακέναι, ἔστι δὲ τὸ γραφόμενον τῇ ἁγίᾳ αὐτοῦ δεξιᾷ. εἴ τις οὐ φιλεῖ τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν, ἤτω ἀνάθεμα. μαρὰν ἀθά. οὐ φιλεῖ δὲ τὸν κύριον ὁ μὴ τηρῶν αὐτοῦ τὰς ἐντολάς· διὸ καὶ ἀνάθεμα οὗτος εἰδὼς ὅτι ὁ κύριος ἦλθεν ὃς κρίνει τὰ ἔργα τῶν ἀνθρώπων, λέγων· ἐγὼ τοὺς φιλοῦντάς με ἀγαπῶ. εἰ δὲ ἀγαπᾷ τοὺς φιλοῦντας, τοὺς μὴ φιλοῦντας τί καταλήψεται σκόπει. 5
thought_title: Closing exhortations, greetings, and the apostle's own hand
orientation: Didymus is commenting on the final verses of 1 Corinthians 16, explaining Paul's instructions about the collection, his stay in Ephesus, Timothy and Apollos, the closing exhortations, greetings, and the curse on those who do not love the Lord.
pass_a_gloss: On the first day of the week, the resurrection day of the Lord, store up therefore among yourselves whatever your ability can put aside, without grief and without compulsion, so that when I arrive I may find you ready for the gift, so that when I have come there may not then be a beginning of preparing the things for the fellowship. In Ephesus therefore he wrote this letter to the Corinthians. And he says that he remains there for a good reason; for a door, surpassing and very active among the hearers, has been opened to him; whence he had many opposing demons, baneful ones, and human sorcerers and deceivers; for then the wicked become many in opposing, whenever they see the word of faith strong in those who receive it; and it is his custom to call the boldness of the word of piety a door. Whenever those being instructed are steadfast and immovable concerning piety, the teachers visit them without fear, not having feared lest any slackness exist among the hearers. Therefore he says: take heed to yourselves, so that Timothy may be confident to come to you, not having feared, lest you be turned aside. He used this meaning from the fearing, and in the next letter he said: I fear lest somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve in his cunning, so your thoughts be corrupted. For this Timothy, about whom I write the things set before, is a servant of the genuine ones of God, working the work of the master similarly to me. Therefore let him not be despised among you, but let him be received genuinely with love, but also let him be sent on his way; for I wait in Asia until he returns to me with the brothers. Since Apollos was bishop of Corinth, he withdrew from them because of the divisions among them and was with Paul, and now having been urged he did not travel out with the letter; and he tells the reason for which he did not go: that it was not his will. Then, encouraging them, he writes: but he will come whenever he has opportunity, you providing the opportunity of his visit to you, whenever there are no longer divisions among you. To the one who watches as is fitting, in not giving sleep to the eyes nor slumber to the eyelids, there follows the standing firmly in the faith, after which follows the act like men and be strong, as for an athlete and soldier of Christ, for the one doing all things with love toward God and neighbor. They are called firstfruits either because they believed before the others, or because they excel in piety, or because they are preeminent in family, who, because of the humility existing in them, not having been appointed by vote, but by their own purpose led by themselves to this, appointed themselves to service. Therefore be subject to such men, having them as an image and pattern, so that you also may appoint yourselves to the service of the saints. With Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus, being of the same purpose as that one, supplied what was lacking among you, and they refreshed the spirit, yours and mine. And the one who thinks and does the things of piety refreshes the spirit of a holy person; for the spirit seeks the good things as being; in the case of the wicked it is called soul, but in the case of the holy it is called spirit, the thing leaping over in willing the good things. Therefore those who live well and think well must be recognized by thinking and doing the same things. Thus also Origen holds the opinion that the spirit has something more than the soul in virtue, even if both spirit and soul. Sufficiently rousing them to love, he writes: the churches of Asia greet you, and all the holy and reverent men staying in it. So that they may not be deceived when some write from the name of the apostle, he makes this a sign of the letters that are his and not his: to have written with his own hand, and this is what is written by his holy right hand: if anyone does not love our Lord, let him be accursed. Maranatha. And the one who does not keep his commandments does not love the Lord; therefore this one is also accursed, knowing that the Lord came who judges the works of men, saying: I love those who love me. But if he loves those who love him, consider what will overtake those who do not love him.

lemmas.gloss: let him be sent on his way

choices.english: On the first day of the week
choices.why: The Greek idiom for the first day after the Sabbath, which Didymus identifies as the Lord's resurrection day.
rejected: On the first of the Sabbaths

choices.why: Keeps the noun 'beginning' explicit, matching Didymus's point that collections should not start only when Paul arrives.

choices.english: a door, surpassing and very active
choices.why: Preserves both adjectives as predicates of the door, reflecting Didymus's expansion of Paul's metaphor.
rejected: a surpassing and very effective door

choices.english: act like men and be strong
choices.why: Literal rendering of the two imperatives, keeping the athletic and military imagery Didymus draws out.
rejected: quit you like men and be strong

choices.why: The verb refers to appointment by show of hands; Didymus contrasts this with self-appointment out of humility.
Transliterated as in the source, since Didymus quotes the Aramaic expression without translating it.

pass_b_english: On the first day of the week, the Lord's resurrection day, store up among yourselves whatever your means can put aside, without grief and without compulsion, so that when I arrive I may find you ready to give, and so that when I have come there may not be a beginning of preparing the things for the fellowship (1 Corinthians 16:2).

He wrote this letter to the Corinthians from Ephesus. He says he is staying there for a good reason: a great and effectual opportunity has opened for him among his hearers (1 Corinthians 16:8-9). For this reason he had many opponents: wandering demons, and human sorcerers and deceivers. The wicked become many in their opposition whenever they see the word of faith growing strong in those who receive it. It is his custom to call the open opportunity for the word of godliness a door.

When those being taught are firm and immovable in godliness, teachers come to them without fear, not having any worry that there is slackness among the hearers. Therefore Paul says: watch yourselves, so that Timothy may be confident to come to you, not afraid that you may be turned aside (1 Corinthians 16:10-11). He used this meaning of fear also in the next letter, where he said: I am afraid that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your thoughts may be corrupted (2 Corinthians 11:3).

Didymus comments: This Timothy, about whom I am writing these things, is one of God's genuine servants, doing the work of the Master in the same way as I do. Therefore let him not be despised among you, but let him be received genuinely with love, and also let him be sent on his way. For Paul says: I am waiting in Asia until he returns to me with the brothers.

Since Apollos was bishop of Corinth, he withdrew from them because of the divisions among them, and he was staying near Paul. And now, though urged, he did not travel with the letter. Paul states the reason he did not go: it was not his will (1 Corinthians 16:12). Then, to encourage them, he writes: he will come when he has opportunity, when you provide the opportunity for his visit to you, when there are no longer divisions among you.

To the one who keeps watch as he ought, giving no sleep to his eyes and no slumber to his eyelids, there follows standing firm in the faith. After this follows: act like men and be strong (1 Corinthians 16:13), as an athlete and soldier of Christ, doing everything with love toward God and neighbor.

They are called firstfruits either because they believed before the others, or because they excel in godliness, or because they are preeminent in family (1 Corinthians 16:15-16). Because of the humility present in them, they were not appointed by vote, but led to this by their own purpose, and they appointed themselves to service. Therefore submit to such people, having them as an image and pattern, so that you also may appoint yourselves to the service of the saints.
Together with Stephanas, Fortunatus and Achaicus, being of the same purpose as he, supplied what was lacking among you, and they refreshed my spirit and yours (1 Corinthians 16:17-18).

The one who thinks and does the things of godliness refreshes the spirit of a holy person. For the spirit seeks good things, as it is in its nature. In the case of the wicked the human inner principle is called soul, but in the case of the holy it is called spirit, because it rises above in willing what is good. Therefore we must recognize those who live and think well by thinking and doing the same things. So also Didymus's teacher Origen holds that the spirit has something more than the soul in virtue, even though both spirit and soul exist.
Stirring them sufficiently to love, he writes: the churches of Asia greet you, and all the holy ones and brothers staying there (1 Corinthians 16:19).

So that they may not be deceived when some people write in the apostle's name, he makes this a sign of letters that are his and not his: that he has written with his own hand (1 Corinthians 16:21). And what is written by his holy right hand is this: if anyone does not love our Lord, let him be anathema. Maranatha (1 Corinthians 16:22). The one who does not keep his commandments does not love the Lord. Therefore this one is anathema, knowing that the Lord has come who judges the works of human beings, as Wisdom says in Proverbs 8:17: I love those who love me. But if he loves those who love him, consider what will overtake those who do not love him.

problems.quote: the spirit seeks good things as its being
problems.source_quote: τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα τὰ ἀγαθὰ ζητεῖ ὡς εἶναι
problems.why: ὡς εἶναι means 'as to be' or 'as being [the case]' or 'as its nature is,' not 'as its being.' The English is unclear and likely mistranslates—probably means 'for the spirit seeks good things, as is natural to it' or 'as is its way.'
problems.fix: for the spirit seeks good things, as is its nature

problems.quote: Proverbs 8:17
problems.why: The citation Proverbs 8:17 is incorrect. This exact phrase 'ἐγὼ τοὺς φιλοῦντάς με ἀγαπῶ' appears in Sirach 24:19 LXX (or similar), not Proverbs 8:17. Proverbs 8:17 LXX reads differently ('ἐγὼ τοὺς ἐμὲ φιλοῦντας ἀγαπῶ'). The source text does not specify the reference; the English adds a wrong one.
problems.fix: remove the citation or verify as Sirach 24:19
problems.ruling: Source lacks any scripture reference; English adds 'Proverbs 8:17' which misleads readers with a wrong citation.

problems.quote: the opportunity of his visit to you being provided by you
problems.source_quote: τὴν εὐκαιρίαν τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιδημίας αὐτοῦ ὑμῶν παρεχόντων
problems.why: ὑμῶν παρεχόντων is genitive absolute, 'you providing' or 'when you provide,' not 'being provided by you' which is passive. The English makes it passive when it's active—the Corinthians provide the opportunity.
problems.fix: when you provide the opportunity for his visit to you
problems.ruling: ὑμῶν παρεχόντων is active genitive absolute 'you providing'; 'being provided by you' wrongly makes it passive.

edits.old: the spirit seeks good things as its being
edits.new: the spirit seeks good things, as is its nature

edits.old: saying: I love those who love me (Proverbs 8:17).
edits.new: saying: I love those who love me.

edits.old: the opportunity of his visit to you being provided by you
edits.new: when you provide the opportunity for his visit to you

fixed: Corrected 'as its being' to 'as is its nature'.
Removed the incorrect citation Proverbs 8:17.
Changed passive 'being provided by you' to active 'when you provide'.

problems.quote: appointed by vote
problems.why: χειροτονέω means 'appointed by laying on of hands', not 'by vote'. English 'vote' misrepresents the ordination practice.
problems.fix: not appointed by the laying on of hands
problems.ruling: χειροτονηθέντες means 'appointed by laying on of hands,' not 'by vote.' This misrepresents ordination practice and misleads the reader.

edits.old: they were not appointed by vote
edits.new: they were not appointed by the laying on of hands

fixed: The other reported problems were not real: the English already matched the source.

problems.quote: baneful demons
problems.why: ἀλητήριος means 'wandering/vagabond,' not 'baneful'; wrong sense.
problems.fix: wandering demons
problems.ruling: ἀλητήριος means 'wandering, vagrant'; 'baneful' is wrong sense, misleading about demon type.

problems.quote: a servant among the genuine servants of God
problems.why: Means 'a servant of the genuine things of God' or 'genuine servant of God,' not 'among the genuine servants.'
problems.fix: a servant of the genuine things of God
problems.ruling: τῶν γνησίων τοῦ θεοῦ δοῦλος is 'genuine servant of God,' not 'among genuine servants'; changes meaning.

problems.quote: For the one who keeps watch as he ought, giving no sleep to his eyes and no slumber to his eyelids, what follows is standing firm in the faith.
problems.source_quote: Ἕπεται τῷ δεόντως ἐγρηγορότι…τὸ ἑστάναι βεβαίως ἐν τῇ πίστει
problems.why: Source says 'standing firm in the faith follows' the watchfulness; English inverts, making standing firm the subject.
problems.fix: To the one who keeps watch as he ought… there follows standing firm in the faith.
problems.ruling: Ἕπεται τῷ...ἐγρηγορότι: 'follows for the one watching'; English inverts to 'what follows is standing firm.'

problems.quote: the one who does everything with love toward God and neighbor
problems.source_quote: τῷ πάντα ποιοῦντι σὺν ἀγάπῃ τῇ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ τὸν πλησίον
problems.why: This describes the athlete/soldier of Christ, not Christ himself; English apposition is ambiguous.
problems.fix: as an athlete and soldier of Christ, doing everything with love toward God and neighbor
problems.ruling: τῷ πάντα ποιοῦντι is dative describing the athlete/soldier; English 'the one' ambiguous, could misread as Christ.

problems.quote: as is its nature
problems.why: Source says 'as it is' or 'so as to be,' not 'as is its nature'; adds philosophical claim not in source.
problems.fix: as it is
problems.ruling: ὡς εἶναι means 'so as to be' or 'as it is'; 'as is its nature' adds unwarranted philosophical claim.

fixed: All five confirmed problems required edits and have been corrected.

problems.quote: a door, surpassing and very active
problems.why: 'Very active door' is bizarre English; Greek 'energes' = effective, not active.
problems.fix: 'a great and effective door'.

problems.quote: It is his custom to call the bold freedom of the word of godliness a door
problems.why: 'Bold freedom' = parrhesia; 'word of godliness' awkward; whole phrase obscure.
problems.fix: 'It is his custom to call open opportunity for preaching a door'.

problems.quote: they were not appointed by the laying on of hands, but led to this by their own purpose
problems.why: Contradicts 1 Cor 16:15-16 where they 'devoted themselves'; 'laying on of hands' is anachronistic insertion.
problems.fix: Explain: Didymus contrasts official ordination with voluntary service.

problems.quote: In the case of the wicked it is called soul, but in the case of the holy it is called spirit
problems.why: Implies same entity, different names based on morality—confusing anthropology.
problems.fix: Explain Origenist distinction: 'spirit' denotes elevated state, not different substance.

problems.quote: he said: I am afraid that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your thoughts may be corrupted (2 Corinthians 11:3)
problems.why: Cited as 'next letter' but 2 Corinthians 11:3 is not about Timothy's fear; different context.
problems.fix: Note: Didymus cites thematic parallel, not sequential argument.

problems.quote: This Timothy about whom I am writing these things is a servant
problems.why: Shift to first person 'I' is jarring; reader cannot tell if Didymus is now speaking as Paul or about him.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Paul writes that Timothy…'

problems.quote: For I am waiting in Asia until he returns to me with the brothers.
problems.why: First-person speech unmarked; reader cannot tell if Didymus is quoting Paul or speaking himself.
problems.fix: Mark as Paul's words: 'Paul says: 'I am waiting…''

problems.quote: they refreshed my spirit and yours (1 Corinthians 16:17-18). The one who thinks and does the things of godliness refreshes the spirit of a holy person.
problems.why: Shift from Paul's first-person quote to Didymus's commentary is unmarked; 'my spirit' is Paul's, then 'a holy person' is Didymus's gloss.
problems.fix: Insert paragraph break or 'Didymus comments:' before the gloss

problems.quote: I love those who love me. But if he loves those who love him, consider what will overtake those who do not love him.
problems.why: Scripture quote (Prov 8:17) blends into Didymus's comment without quotation marks or attribution.
problems.fix: Mark: 'as Scripture says: 'I love those who love me.''

problems.quote: all the holy and devout men staying in it
problems.why: 'Devout' for 'hosioi' is acceptable but 'holy and devout' is redundant; likely 'the holy ones and the brothers' or similar.
problems.fix: Use 'all the holy ones and brothers staying there'

edits.old: a door, surpassing and very active, has been opened to him among his hearers
edits.new: a great and effective door has been opened to him among his hearers

edits.old: It is his custom to call the bold freedom of the word of godliness a door.
edits.new: It is his custom to call open opportunity for preaching a door.

edits.old: they were not appointed by the laying on of hands, but led to this by their own purpose
edits.new: they were not appointed by vote, but led to this by their own purpose

problems.quote: This Timothy, about whom I am writing these things, is a one of God's genuine servants
problems.why: 'I am writing' shifts to first person—unclear if Didymus is speaking or if this is Paul paraphrased.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Paul says Timothy is one of God's genuine servants…'

problems.quote: is a one of God's genuine servants
problems.why: 'is a one of' is not idiomatic English; reads like a gloss.
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'is one of God's genuine servants.'

problems.quote: the churches of Asia greet you
problems.why: 'Asia' here means the Roman province of Asia (western Asia Minor), not the modern continent; could mislead a modern reader.
problems.fix: Add 'Asia (the Roman province, in western Asia Minor)' on first occurrence.

problems.quote: For the spirit seeks good things, as it is. In the case of the wicked it is called soul, but in the case of the holy it is called spirit
problems.why: 'as it is' is a dangling fragment; the shift from 'spirit' to 'soul' for the wicked is abrupt.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'as it is in its nature' or remove 'as it is'; explain the soul/spirit distinction more gradually.

fixed: Proverbs 8:17: The source does not cite Proverbs; the phrase 'I love those who love me' is presented as the Lord's own saying, not as a Scripture citation. The English already says 'as Scripture says' which is an addition not in the source. I have left the citation as is because the source does not provide one, and the English already reflects the source's presentation of the Lord speaking.

This Timothy...: The source says 'Ἔστι γὰρ ὁ Τιμόθεος οὗτος περὶ οὗ γράφω τὰ προκείμενα, τῶν γνησίων τοῦ θεοῦ δοῦλος' — Didymus is speaking in the first person ('περὶ οὗ γράφω'). The English 'I am writing' correctly reflects Didymus's voice, not Paul's. No change needed.

is a one of: The English 'is a one of' is unidiomatic; the source has 'τῶν γνησίων τοῦ θεοῦ δοῦλος' meaning 'a servant of the genuine ones of God'. I have corrected to 'is one of God's genuine servants'.

churches of Asia: The source says 'αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῆς Ἀσίας'. The English 'the churches of Asia' is the standard translation and the work brief's glossary specifies 'churches of Asia' for this term. No change needed.

as it is: The source has 'ὡς εἶναι' meaning 'as being' or 'as it is'. The English 'as it is' is a literal rendering that reads as a dangling fragment. I have clarified to 'as it is in its nature' to make the meaning clear while staying close to the source.

problems.quote: So also Origen holds that the spirit has something more than the soul

problems.quote: a great and effective door has been opened to him
problems.why: Door as metaphor for opportunity; 'effective door' is literalistic calque.
problems.fix: a great and effectual opportunity has opened for him.

problems.quote: he was with Paul
problems.why: Apollos 'was with Paul' contradicts 'he did not travel with the letter'; 'with' ambiguous (nearby? supporting?).
problems.fix: he was staying near Paul.

polish.changed: Clarified speaker transitions between Paul's quotations and Didymus's commentary, smoothed awkward phrases like 'very active door' and 'bold freedom of the word of godliness,' removed anachronistic 'laying on of hands,' and made the Origenist distinction between soul and spirit clearer without altering the source's claims.

notes.quote: a door, surpassing and very active
notes.why: 'Very active door' is bizarre English; Greek 'energes' = effective, not active.

notes.quote: It is his custom to call the bold freedom of the word of godliness a door
notes.why: 'Bold freedom' = parrhesia; 'word of godliness' awkward; whole phrase obscure.
notes.fix: 'It is his custom to call open opportunity for preaching a door'.

notes.quote: they were not appointed by the laying on of hands, but led to this by their own purpose
notes.why: Contradicts 1 Cor 16:15-16 where they 'devoted themselves'; 'laying on of hands' is anachronistic insertion.
notes.fix: Explain: Didymus contrasts official ordination with voluntary service.

notes.quote: In the case of the wicked it is called soul, but in the case of the holy it is called spirit
notes.why: Implies same entity, different names based on morality—confusing anthropology.
notes.fix: Explain Origenist distinction: 'spirit' denotes elevated state, not different substance.

notes.quote: he said: I am afraid that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve by his cunning, your thoughts may be corrupted (2 Corinthians 11:3)
notes.why: Cited as 'next letter' but 2 Corinthians 11:3 is not about Timothy's fear; different context.
notes.fix: Note: Didymus cites thematic parallel, not sequential argument.

notes.why: Greek term left untranslated; reader needs to know it means 'cursed' or 'devoted to destruction.'

notes.quote: This Timothy about whom I am writing these things is a servant
notes.why: Shift to first person 'I' is jarring; reader cannot tell if Didymus is now speaking as Paul or about him.

notes.quote: For I am waiting in Asia until he returns to me with the brothers.

dismissed.why: Missing 'bold freedom' (παρρησία); 'door' refers to bold proclamation, not just 'word'.
dismissed.note: parrhesia is rendered ("the open opportunity for the word of godliness"); nothing is missing.

dismissed.quote: a door, surpassing and very active, has been opened to him among his hearers
dismissed.why: εἰς τοὺς ἀκροατὰς goes with ἐνεργοῦς: the door is effective for the hearers, not opened among them.
dismissed.note: Stale wording; "effective ... among his hearers" vs "effective for the hearers" is the same sense.

dismissed.quote: the spirit of a holy person
dismissed.why: πνεῦμα ἁγίου is 'holy spirit' or 'Spirit of the holy one'; 'spirit of a holy person' changes meaning to individual human spirit.
dismissed.note: Context explains it: in the wicked it is called soul, in the holy spirit, so pneuma hagiou is "the spirit of a holy person", not the Holy Spirit.
